prompt.body: 90s hard rock at 148 BPM in A minor. The song is about a band's first open-mic night. Slash's Les Paul, palm-muted chug, fast and aggressive. The vocalist is Axl Rose circa 1987 — screaming into a bar mic, no polish, just a kid with a scream. The drummer is relentless — double-kick throughout, the song is a 3-minute assault. The bass is thick, distorted, palm-muted root notes. The chorus is a gang shout with three-part vocal harmony and dual-guitar octave. Slash-style solo with fast pentatonic runs and a dive-bomb. The lyrics are about a bar on Eighth, fifteen minutes to make them remember, three covers and a half-written song, hands shaking, the barman pouring whiskey, the keyboard player saying we were too loud, the notepad girl, the next week's sign 'no GnR crew.' Think GnR 'You're Crazy' or Skid Row 'Piece of Me' — fast, raw, hungry, the proving ground. The song is the moment the band earned their chops. Production: raw, the Les Paul is overdriven, the drummer is hitting too hard. FIRE.
